action: Treat unexpected texts about a suspended bank card as phishing: do not open the link, and contact your bank through its official channel.
date_note: ZATAZ page last updated 19 November 2026; the article gives the arrest only as November 2026, so the publication day is used.
exec: A fake mobile base station in a car allegedly pushed bank-card phishing texts to phones in central Tokyo; the suspect denies it.
impact: ZATAZ relays a police estimate that more than 10,000 devices were disrupted in under two hours; this is not a confirmed number of people defrauded.
plain: Police in Tokyo arrested a man over a car-mounted fake mobile antenna that allegedly sent phishing texts to phones nearby. He denies it.
summary: ZATAZ reports that a 31-year-old Chinese national was arrested in Tokyo over an SMS blaster in a car in the Ginza district. Police estimate more than 10,000 devices were disrupted in under two hours, with Chinese-language texts saying a bank card was suspended and linking to a payment-details page. The suspect denies the offence and says the car held no radio equipment.
title: Tokyo: man arrested over SMS blaster said to have disrupted 10,000 phones

validation.note: ZATAZ read; the police figures are relayed, not read at the police or Japanese outlets.
